object_context: Finite-to-global spectral stability obstruction for the Riemann Hypothesis spectral lane: determine a non-circular convergence package that can carry independently defined finite/restricted self-adjoint or real-zero approximants to the exact Riemann Xi entire function or complete zeta-zero spectrum, with multiplicity and without spectral pollution, escaped/missing zeros, order-of-limits ambiguity, or post-hoc normalization.
structural_coordinates: the target is the fixed nonzero entire Riemann Xi function, not merely a zero-counting asymptotic or finite prefix of its zeros

Connes-Consani-Moscovici 2025 construct finite/restricted self-adjoint operators whose approximant entire-function zeros are real and equal the approximant spectra under explicit simple/even ground-state hypotheses
Suzuki 2026 constructs finite-interval self-adjoint realizations and formulates the target zeta-spectrum operator as an a-to-infinity limit conjecture

local-uniform convergence of nonzero holomorphic/entire approximants is qualitatively different from pointwise convergence of selected zeros, zero-counting convergence, or convergence of spectral measures
for a sequence of real-rooted entire functions, local-uniform convergence to a nonzero entire limit gives a direct Hurwitz-type route to excluding nonreal zeros of the limit
self-adjointness of every approximating operator does not by itself identify the spectrum of an infinite-cutoff limit
Galerkin/projection approximations of self-adjoint operators can exhibit spectral pollution, so an operator-topology claim must include hypotheses that exclude spurious or missing spectral points
norm-resolvent, strong-resolvent, form/Mosco, local-uniform determinant, and spectral-measure convergence preserve different information and are not interchangeable
the RH approximants may vary in Hilbert space, cutoff, finite-dimensional subspace, prime range, ground state, and determinant normalization, so comparison maps and joint-limit order are load-bearing
the simple/even ground-state hypotheses used in finite-parameter real-zero operator theorems must be proved uniformly/cofinally or explicitly replaced

the arithmetic side must converge to the full Weil/Guinand explicit-formula data including all prime-power and archimedean contributions; a purely spectral topology is insufficient if the target identity is not bound
multiplicity, zero completeness on arbitrary compact sets, absence of spectral escape, and absence of spurious limits are separate proof obligations
equivalent_formulations: prove that a canonically normalized family of real-rooted approximant entire functions F_alpha converges locally uniformly on C to Xi and that the limit is nonzero
prove convergence of normalized regularized determinants of independently defined self-adjoint approximants to Xi in a topology strong enough for Hurwitz zero transport on every compact subset

construct a common/direct-limit Hilbert-space realization in which self-adjoint approximants converge with additional compactness/spectral exactness sufficient to identify the complete limiting point spectrum with the zeta-zero ordinates

prove compact-by-compact convergence of the complete approximant zero multisets to the Xi zero multiset with multiplicity, together with an arithmetic theorem identifying the limiting entire function as Xi
falsify the current route by showing that its natural approximants necessarily violate a required uniform ground-state, normalization, compactness, or spectral-exactness condition
solved_analogues: Hurwitz-type zero stability for locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions: off the real axis, a locally uniform nonzero limit of functions having no zeros there remains zero-free
finite-dimensional and compact-operator spectral approximation under strong enough norm/compactness hypotheses, where isolated eigenvalues and multiplicities can be controlled
near_solved_analogues: Connes-van Suijlekom 2025 real-zero theorem plus Connes-Consani-Moscovici 2025 finite-prime spectral triples: the approximant real-zero/self-adjointness mechanism is rigorous while convergence to Xi/zeta zeros is open
Suzuki 2026 screw-function construction: finite-interval self-adjoint operators are rigorous while the a-to-infinity zeta-spectrum operator limit is conjectural

self-adjoint Galerkin spectral approximation: mature theory precisely characterizes spectral pollution and supplies hostile examples showing that well-posed finite approximants can have spurious spectral limits
Yang-Mills YM-S1d in current RAKL main: a separate Millennium lane independently isolates finite-regulator-to-continuum spectral identification and physical scaling as non-compensatory obligations

method_transfers.source_context: Hurwitz zero-stability and the Connes-van Suijlekom real-zero framework
method_transfers.method: replace vague spectral convergence by local-uniform convergence of canonically normalized entire functions whose finite-stage zeros are already known to be real, then use zero-stability on every off-real compact region
shared_structure: each approximant has a rigorously controlled zero set
the target is an entire function
root authority concerns exclusion of nonreal zeros globally
required_assumptions: every approximant in the chosen cofinal family satisfies the real-zero theorem hypotheses
one fixed source-side normalization is defined before comparing with Xi
the normalized approximants converge locally uniformly on the full complex plane
the limit is exactly Xi and is not the zero function
disanalogies: the hard arithmetic work is precisely to prove local-uniform convergence to Xi; Hurwitz does not supply that convergence
operator convergence and determinant convergence need not be equivalent without additional trace-class/regularization control
method_transfers.repair_question: What exact uniform estimates on the restricted Weil forms, ground states and regularized determinants would imply local-uniform convergence of the normalized approximant entire functions to Xi?
source_anchors: Alain Connes and Walter D. van Suijlekom, Quadratic Forms, Real Zeros and Echoes of the Spectral Action, arXiv:2511.23257 (2025)
Alain Connes, Caterina Consani, Henri Moscovici, Zeta Spectral Triples, arXiv:2511.22755 (2025)

method_transfers.source_context: self-adjoint operator convergence and compact spectral approximation
method_transfers.method: embed or identify approximating Hilbert spaces, choose an operator/form convergence topology, and add compactness/spectral-exactness hypotheses strong enough to transport isolated eigenvalues with multiplicity
shared_structure: a family of self-adjoint operators is intended to approach a limiting self-adjoint operator
the desired conclusion is spectral rather than merely weak convergence of matrix elements
multiplicity and exclusion of spurious spectral points are load-bearing
required_assumptions: common Hilbert-space identification or a rigorously defined varying-space convergence framework
specified norm/strong resolvent or form convergence
compactness or another theorem excluding spectral pollution/escape in the region used
the limiting operator is independently identified and has the target spectral determinant or spectrum
disanalogies: the RH constructions use changing cutoffs/finite subspaces and may not present a single obvious common domain
even exact operator convergence would not identify the zeta spectrum unless the arithmetic determinant/trace bridge is also proved
method_transfers.repair_question: Is there a common-space or varying-space convergence theorem naturally matched to the Weil-form approximants that simultaneously gives operator convergence and spectral exactness on arbitrary bounded spectral windows?
source_anchors: Tosio Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators
Michael Levitin and Eugene Shargorodsky, Spectral pollution and second order relative spectra for self-adjoint operators, arXiv:math/0212087 / IMA J. Numer. Anal. 24 (2004)

method_transfers.method: before proving a positive RH limit theorem, build projection/self-adjoint known-answer examples where finite spectra converge misleadingly, and require the proposed topology/hypotheses to reject every such example
shared_structure: risk that apparently stable low eigenvalues do not represent the true target spectrum
required_assumptions: counterexamples preserve the structural coordinates relevant to the claimed convergence theorem
the rejection criterion is theorem-level rather than numerical pattern matching
disanalogies: standard Galerkin pollution often concerns gaps in essential spectrum, whereas a successful RH operator may have a different global spectral type
a pollution counterexample can refute a convergence package but cannot prove the arithmetic route correct
method_transfers.repair_question: Which weakest additional compactness, second-order spectral, determinant, or zero-stability condition rules out the hostile pollution/escape examples while remaining plausible for the RH approximants?

method_transfers.method: decompose a seductive finite-regulator statement into separate uniformity, physical scaling, spectral visibility and continuum-identification obligations before treating the finite result as root evidence
shared_structure: rigorous finite/regulator-level spectral information exists or is sought
the root statement concerns an infinite/global limiting theory
weak convergence can lose the exact spectral property needed at the root
required_assumptions: the common abstraction is limited to finite-to-global spectral transport
no Yang-Mills theorem or physical scaling statement is transferred to RH
each RH obligation is re-derived in its own entire-function/operator setting
disanalogies: Yang-Mills has lattice spacing, volume, gauge reconstruction and physical units; RH has prime/interval cutoffs, entire functions and arithmetic trace identities
a mass-gap lower bound and a complete zeta-zero multiset are different spectral targets
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the same non-compensatory obligation discipline expose exactly which RH finite-to-global step fails without importing any Yang-Mills mathematical claim?

explicit_disanalogies: local-uniform convergence of normalized entire determinants is sufficient only after the approximant real-zero property and exact Xi limit are proved; it cannot be inferred from numerical zero accuracy
strong-resolvent or Mosco convergence by itself is not declared sufficient for complete spectral exactness; additional compactness/no-pollution hypotheses must be identified
self-adjointness at every finite stage does not imply self-adjointness or spectral identity of an unspecified limit
convergence of the first k zeros for each fixed k does not by itself control all zeros uniformly or identify multiplicities
post-hoc determinant normalizations fitted using known zeta zeros are circular and are excluded
the Yang-Mills continuum-gap analogy transfers only obligation structure, not theorem content
spectral pollution results from projection methods are falsification calibrations, not evidence that the RH approximants actually pollute

cross_domain_analogies.source_kind: numerical spectral approximation / engineering model reduction
cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A sequence of finite, internally stable models can display plausible eigenvalues while failing to approximate the full spectrum of the infinite system; convergence requires a specified topology plus stability/compactness conditions that rule out spurious modes and escaped modes.
common_abstraction: finite/restricted models approximate a global object
each finite model can be mathematically well posed
the target property is spectral and can be lost under weak convergence
a validation suite must distinguish true convergence from finite-prefix fit
source_to_target_mapping: finite discretization/model -> finite-prime or finite-interval RH operator
spurious numerical mode -> spectral pollution/spurious limiting zero
unresolved high-frequency mode -> escaped or missing zeta zero
mesh/refinement stability theorem -> cutoff/parameter convergence theorem
known-answer convergence benchmark -> hostile RH limit-stability calibration
shared_constraints: the finite model must be defined independently of the target spectrum
the refinement parameter and comparison map must be explicit
the theorem must control the property actually claimed, not only a proxy norm/statistic
negative calibration examples must be structurally relevant to the proposed convergence package
disanalogies: the Riemann Xi target is a fixed arithmetic entire function rather than an experimentally observed physical system
RH additionally requires exact prime/archimedean arithmetic matching, not just numerical spectral fidelity
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Treat every finite-stage spectral success as provisional until a named convergence topology and no-pollution/completeness theorem transports the exact arithmetic object to the global target; use hostile spectral-approximation examples to falsify insufficient convergence packages first.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For each proposed RH convergence package, prove it rejects explicit self-adjoint spectral-pollution/escape counterexamples, then prove the package from the actual Weil-form/operator family with a source-side normalization and exact arithmetic Xi identification.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only analogy grounded in spectral approximation theory and the current Yang-Mills finite-to-continuum obligation pattern; it supplies no evidence for RH.
